load.why: Thread llama-bench runs at 98% while the GPU is 2% busy. Everything waits on this one thread; use --cpu-profile to see what it does.

setup.why: 0.20 s is too short for the GPU's utilization counter. Use a longer run.

warmup.why: 3.2 CPU cores are busy while the GPU is 11% busy: the work is on the CPU.

prefill.why: GPU 59% busy while thread llama-bench runs at 97%: the host is working or spinning on a wait during the GPU's idle part. --nsys shows the gaps, --cpu-profile what the host does.

decode.why: GPU 80% busy while thread llama-bench runs at 99%: the host is working or spinning on a wait during the GPU's idle part. --nsys shows the gaps, --cpu-profile what the host does.

memory.text: 16.21 GiB of mapped files stay in RAM during decode. These pages are reclaimable page cache, not a leak, but they are why a later run loads fast and why the machine shows little free RAM.

movement.text: The model is on hdd storage (<path>/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-Q8_0-upstream.gguf). This run did not read it from disk; --cold-start measures what a first load costs.
The model was 100% in the page cache, so this load time is a warm one. A cold start reads it from disk and takes longer.
5.08 MiB per token crosses NVLink during prefill.

About 58.8 MiB crosses PCIe per token during decode: 12,112 MiB toward the GPUs and 10,458 MiB back. That is tensors moving between RAM and GPU (partial offload, CPU-side layers), a collective going through host memory, or a GPU polling host memory. --nsys gives the exact bytes of real copies, and whatever remains is the other two.
21.59 MiB per token crosses NVLink during decode.

timeline.text: prefill: 55% of host CPU samples are inside the GPU driver (submitting, or spinning on a wait). Hottest functions outside it: dequantize_row_q8_0 29% on 1 thread (at most 29% of the phase).
